questions.explanation: The paradox of austerity was popularized by the famous economist John Maynard Keynes. According to Keynes, during economic recession individuals try to save more, which inevitably leads to a decline in aggregate demand and hence economic growth. Such a situation is harmful for everyone as investments give lower returns than normal. Keynes further said that such a large increase in saving ultimately hurts the economy as a whole. This theory was heavily criticized by non- Keynesian economists on the grounds that an increase in savings allows banks to lend more. This will reduce interest rates and increase borrowing and, hence, increase spending.
